agree.reason: Marisol gets a clear, believable case for the van, but the late-report apology comes with no reporting commitment, so the reader who chased that report has little reason to expect better this time.

honest.reason: The draft rightly drops the unsupported 'double' claim, but two lines go further than the facts: 'at least 9,000 additional pounds' (the brief says the offer was roughly 9,000) and 'the same offers will come next summer'.

works_the_facts.reason: The derived figures are correct and well chosen: 62 lb per household, fresh food under one-sixth of the total, 3,000 lb a month as 'half again' the current fresh amount, about 5 lb per household, and the 26% local share; it does not mention the van's running costs.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is put concretely as turning down the farm produce again, though the draft states as certain that the offers will come back.

qualification.reason: The target can be checked against monthly distribution figures, but no reporting date is given and nothing is said about what happens if the 9,000 lb isn't reached.

objections.reason: The late report is admitted openly but not fixed (for example, by promising quarterly updates on set dates), and nothing answers the obvious question of how the van will be run and maintained once reserves are down to $11,000.

fit.reason: It's a well-organized grant narrative of about 390 words, comfortably within the 500-word limit.
